text: Henry Nolan’s motive to evoke nostalgia and a sense of belonging is structurally reinforced by his use of the old mill as a central metaphor. By positioning the mill as a symbol of stability and resistance against modernity, the thematic structure of the text contrasts the enduring value of tradition and community with the disruptive forces of change. This structural opposition serves the author's intent by grounding the abstract concepts of belonging and tradition in a tangible, steadfast image, thereby highlighting the tension between the past and the present.
